question.text: Which of the following correctly represents the variation of electric potential <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo><mi>V</mi><mo>)</mo></math> of a charged spherical conductor of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo><mi>R</mi><mo>)</mo></math> with radial distance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>)</mo></math> from the centre?

solution.text:
As electric field inside the charged conducting sphere is zero, therefore potential will be constant for the inside part.

For outside part, electric potential decreases as V=kqr and the conducting sphere behaves like a point charge concentrated at the centre.
